narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and unfortunately, we were unable to approve it at this time. The decision was based on several key factors in your financial profile that, when considered together, suggested a higher risk of difficulty repaying the loan. While your request was for 1,344 Deutsche Marks—a smaller amount than the average approved loan of 2,887 DM—other aspects of your situation raised concerns.

The most significant factor was the status of your checking account. Unlike most approved applicants, who typically have at least some funds in their account, yours currently shows a negative balance. This was the strongest signal that influenced the decision, as it may indicate recent financial strain. Additionally, the purpose of your loan—financing a new car—was another factor that worked against approval. While many loans are granted for essentials like home furnishings or repairs, new car loans are slightly riskier in the eyes of the model, as they’re often seen as more discretionary.

On a more positive note, the relatively short repayment period you requested (12 months, compared to the average of 19 months) actually helped your case, as shorter loans are generally less risky. However, this benefit wasn’t enough to offset the other concerns. Your credit history, which includes past payment delays, also played a role, though it wasn’t one of the top factors in this decision.

To improve your chances in the future, focusing on stabilizing your checking account balance and addressing any past credit issues could make a meaningful difference. If possible, waiting until your account is in better standing or exploring a smaller loan amount might also help. We understand this isn’t the outcome you hoped for, and we encourage you to review your financial situation before reapplying.
